title: FMS Aqua
description: The management system behind GreenFeed’s fish farms, in daily use across about 40 ponds since September 2026. It covers production, planning, materials, and feed and supply inventory, and integrates with Solomon. Its reconciliation view checks every warehouse issue against what each pond actually consumed, so gaps show up the same day.

title: FMS
description: The system that runs daily operations at GreenFeed’s 32 pig farms for about 1,000 users, from production and planning to sales and transport. I was one of three engineers on the Sales module, which turns a weighed pig into an order, a price, and an e-invoice (around 130 a day) and hands the final transaction to SAP. Unit prices come from SAP and weights straight from the scale software, replacing Excel sheets and paper slips, and stock and pig status update the moment a sale closes.

title: Transaction Counter
description: The counter system 70 FPT Telecom branches use for contract transactions (new contracts, address changes, and internet plan changes), around 200–300 a day. In a two-person team I built backend and frontend and moved business rules into stored procedures, so they could change without a rebuild and every query stayed inside the DBA team’s 20-second timeout on telecom-scale data. Later I helped rebuild it on .NET 6 microservices with Redis caching and logs shipped through Kafka to Kibana.

title: DBL Store
description: An online store for Dragon Ball Legends game accounts with 800 users and 1,433 orders so far. I built it end to end, from the storefront and API to deployment on a VPS with Docker. Customers sign in with Google, top up points, pick an account within their budget, and receive it instantly.
